subtheme: Keeping model secrets and user privacy safe

subsubthemes.name: Adding noise to protect privacy
subsubthemes.gist: These papers add mathematical noise or perturbations to training data or gradients to hide individual contributions, making it hard for attackers to extract secrets.

subsubthemes.name: Training across many devices without sharing data
subsubthemes.gist: These papers train models on separate machines or users' devices without moving the raw data to a central server, so personal information stays local.

subsubthemes.name: Detecting when models remember private examples
subsubthemes.gist: These papers test whether models memorized specific training examples and reveal them when prompted, using attacks to measure how much privacy was lost.

subsubthemes.name: Keeping secrets in language models and generated content
subsubthemes.gist: These papers stop large language models and diffusion models from leaking training data, or protect privacy when generating synthetic text and images.

subsubthemes.name: Encryption and secure calculations
subsubthemes.gist: These papers use cryptography to let models learn and run without anyone seeing the actual data, keeping computations private end-to-end.

subsubthemes.name: Privacy risks in specific learning tasks
subsubthemes.gist: These papers study how privacy leaks in specialized settings like embeddings, graph learning, federated medical imaging, or when adapting pre-trained models.

subsubthemes.name: Testing and improving privacy guarantees
subsubthemes.gist: These papers measure whether privacy claims are correct, design privacy audits, and improve how we count privacy loss across training steps.
